ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The attached image is a circuit diagram. In the upper left there is a horizontal 2 Ω resistor, with its two ends labeled as “+” on the left side and “-” on the right side, and the voltage is 6 V; the right end of this resistor is connected to the upper node. This upper node is connected downward through a vertical 2 Ω resistor to the bottom node; on the right side there is also a vertical 4 Ω resistor connected between the same upper node and bottom node, with an arrow labeled current I beside it pointing upward. Reasoning: Take the bottom node as the reference point, and let the upper node voltage be V. There is 6 V across the upper-left 2 Ω resistor, with the left side positive and the upper-node side negative, so the current through this resistor is 6/2 = 3 A, in the direction flowing from left to right into the upper node. The current of the middle 2 Ω resistor flowing from the upper node to the bottom node is V/2, and the current of the right-side 4 Ω resistor flowing from the upper node to the bottom node is V/4. Write KCL for the upper node: 3 = V/2 + V/4, therefore 3 = 3V/4, obtaining V = 4 V. The actual downward current in the right-side 4 Ω resistor is V/4 = 1 A, but the reference direction of I in the figure is upward, so I = -1 A.

method.method_draft: First describe the image structure, then solve by node current balance. Treat the bottom node as reference. The upper-left 2 Ω resistor has 6 V across it with the left side positive and the top node side negative, so the current through it is 6/2 = 3 A flowing into the top node. The middle 2 Ω and right 4 Ω resistors both connect from the top node to the bottom node, so if the top-node voltage is V, their downward currents are V/2 and V/4. KCL gives 3 = V/2 + V/4, hence V = 4 V. The current through the 4 Ω resistor is therefore 1 A downward, but the labeled I arrow points upward, so I = -1 A.
